title: Declare each train's themes explicitly, primary theme first

facts.note: Train and wagon definition files are identifiable by path/kind in the planning area; wagon files matter because a wagon's theme and membership feed its train's theme fit.
Fires when a train is authored or edited, or when a wagon is created, edited, deleted, or moved between trains.
Planning tasks that mention trains, themes, or adding/removing/moving/re-theming wagons.

values: train touched while lacking an explicit themes list
wagon added to or moved into a train
wagon removed from or moved out of a train (affects source and destination trains)
train themes list added, removed, changed or reordered
theme of an existing member wagon changed (in the wagon file or elsewhere)
facts.note: Diff-level observer over train and wagon files; must resolve every train whose membership, themes list or member-wagon themes changed, including the train a wagon left.
Detector reads each train: flags a missing/empty explicit themes list; separately reports how many member wagons match the first declared theme.

fires: Planner creates a new train and assigns wagons to it
Planner touches a train that has no explicit themes list (missing declaration must be fixed, not skipped)
Planner adds or moves wagons into an existing train whose primary theme differs from the new wagons' theme
Planner removes a wagon from a train, or moves a wagon out of one train into another (both trains are rechecked)
Planner reorders a train's themes list, changing which theme is primary
Planner changes the theme of an existing wagon that belongs to a train, even when the train file itself is not edited
doesNotFire: Editing a wagon's acceptances without changing its theme or train membership
Editing code or tests outside planning artifacts
Validating that a theme name is canonical (covered by planner.theme.must-be-canonical)

given: A train groups themed wagons and may not yet declare a themes list.
when: You create a train, touch one lacking an explicit themes list, change its themes or their order, add/remove/move its wagons, or re-theme a member wagon.
then: The train declares its themes explicitly as a list whose first entry is its primary theme.
prefer: Most wagons should match the primary (first declared) theme; keep it so when adding, moving or re-theming wagons.
For a train spanning multiple themes, list the dominant theme first, others after as secondary.
On a move, recheck both the train left and the train joined.
avoid: Themes only implied by the train's name or wagons.
Letting most wagons drift to a secondary or undeclared theme.
Listing many secondary themes just to make off-theme wagons look aligned.
unless: Secondary themes are allowed when a train spans multiple themes; not every wagon needs to match the primary.
why: The primary theme is the first declared theme, so it exists only if themes are declared explicitly; most wagons matching it keeps the train coherent.
evidence: Each affected train has an explicit, non-empty themes list; its first entry is the primary theme.
For each affected train, the count/ratio of member wagons matching the primary theme is reported (source: most should match).
verifier_detail: Term theme_alignment: primary theme is the first declared theme; most wagons match it.
Source example (single theme, illustrative): train:orders:checkout -> themes:[orders] (all wagons orders). This illustrates one aligned train; the general standard is 'most', not 'all'.

Majority alignment is phrased in the source as 'should'; 'most' is not quantified. Report the matching ratio (reading 'most' as more than half) rather than inventing a stricter threshold or presenting it as this rule's mandatory gate.
A train with a missing or empty themes list is flagged (train_themes_not_declared); do not treat it as unknown/exempt.
Recheck every train whose membership changed (including the source train of a moved or removed wagon) and every train containing a wagon whose theme changed, not only trains whose file changed.

Source statement (verbatim): A train declares its themes explicitly; most wagons should match the primary declared theme; secondary themes are allowed when a train spans multiple themes.

splitSuggestion.then: Most of a train's wagons should match its primary (first declared) theme; secondary themes are allowed when the train spans multiple themes.

additions.text: Majority alignment ('most wagons should match the primary declared theme') is a separate obligation; proposed as planner.train.primary-theme-majority. In this rule it is kept at its source strength ('should') in prefer[0]/avoid[1].
additions.justification: One obligation per then; explicit declaration is the primary, unconditionally-stated obligation and the precondition for a primary theme to exist.

additions.text: 'Most' read as more than half for reporting; ratio reported, not a stricter threshold.
additions.justification: Source leaves 'most' unquantified; plain-language reading needed for consistent reporting without strengthening the 'should'.

additions.text: Missing/empty themes list is flagged; recheck source and destination trains on moves/removals and trains containing re-themed wagons.
additions.justification: Operational consequences of the source statement; membership and wagon themes can change outside the train file.

additions.text: On a move, recheck both trains.
additions.justification: Removing a wagon can shift the source train's majority; operational consequence, not a new obligation.

additions.text: Listing many secondary themes just to make off-theme wagons look aligned.
additions.justification: Metric-gaming anti-pattern implied by the secondary-theme allowance; keeps the exception non-exploitable.

additions.text: Rationale phrased as train coherence with its declared primary theme.
additions.justification: Source gives no explicit rationale; restates the source term (primary = first declared; most wagons match) without new causal claims.

additions.text: Theme canonicality is covered by planner.theme.must-be-canonical.
additions.justification: Derived from graph.json requires-edge, to keep scope boundaries clear.
